$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{e}^{2x}) \\  & =2{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{xy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{e}^{2x}) \\  & =4{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}

For instance, the function $f(x,y,z)= z\cos(xy)$ has the first-order partial derivative

$$
f_y(x,y,z) = -xz \sin(xy)
$$

and the second-order partial derivative

$$
f_{yx}(x,y,z)= -x yz \cos{\left(x y \right)} - z\sin{\left(x y \right)}.
$$

If we differentiate again, with respect to $x,$ then we get the **third-order partial derivative** $f_{yxx}\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yxx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yx}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-xyz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-z\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-yz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-xyz(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\cdot y)-z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\cdot y \\  & =x{y}^{2}z\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-2yz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

In general, to compute a $n$th-order partial derivative, we need to compute a sequence of $n$ individual derivatives." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124726 :activity/expected-seconds 960.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]
